title: A Summit for the Trail
premise: Vesper Joubert has spent a decade outrunning his family's name and the wreck of his father's salvage company, flying medicine runs into the northern interior. When dying prospector Amos Kettle trades him a map to the Meridian Star — the lost ship that sank Vesper's father's fleet — for a promise to deliver its truth, Vesper is forced back into the world he fled. Racing the salvage fleet run by his estranged uncle, Vesper gathers an unlikely crew who become the family he never had, only to discover the map's real secret: his father scuttled the ship himself to hide evidence of a betrayal that ruins them all. In the final confrontation at the wreck, Vesper must choose between claiming the inheritance that would restore his name and honoring Amos's promise by telling the whole truth — he chooses truth, loses the fortune, and gains a crew, a home airstrip, and a reason to stop moving.
about_author: T. M. Eriksen is a former floatplane mechanic who spent six seasons in remote northern bush camps before turning to writing full-time. Their fiction draws on firsthand knowledge of interior aviation and the tight, improvised communities that form at the edge of the map.

chapters.title: Weather Holds
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A medicine run through worsening weather establishes his restless competence and his rule against staying anywhere too long. He delivers insulin to a river camp, overhears rumors of a salvage fleet buying up charts, and shrugs it off. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as discipline.

chapters.title: The Dying Man's Bargain
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. At a trapping cabin he finds Amos Kettle, injured and feverish, who offers a hand-drawn map to the Meridian Star in exchange for one promise: deliver what's in her hold to the people she was stolen from. Vesper takes the map mostly to save the man's dignity. Beat: reluctant compassion.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Amos's POV, his last days. He explains the dry season will drop the river low enough to reach the wreck — but the salvage fleet's dredges arrive first, and they work for Vesper's uncle, Corvin Joubert. Amos dies at dawn holding Vesper to the promise. Beat: weight of a promise accepted.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. His plane's engine throws a rod on takeoff, stranding him in the river town of Halfway Landing — the exact kind of stopping he avoids. To repair it he must trade labor and favors, meeting mechanic Sefa Tuilagi and deckhand Junie Marsh. Beat: forced stillness, first sparks of found family.

chapters.title: What the Name Buys
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. She recognizes the Joubert name from salvage lore and tests Vesper's story, catching his evasions about his father. Meanwhile Corvin's agents post notices claiming all river wrecks under company title. Beat: trust extended cautiously despite lies of omission.

chapters.title: The Map Is Wrong
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Studying Amos's map against old survey charts, Vesper realizes the marked channel doesn't exist — unless the river shifted after a flood decades ago. The wreck may lie under silt where no one thinks to dig. Beat: hope sharpened by doubt.

chapters.title: Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa agrees to come along if Vesper pays in honesty; Junie signs on for a cut; disgraced river pilot Odile Brant joins when Vesper offers her a chance to clear her name after a wrecking she didn't cause. Beat: a crew assembled from people the industry discarded.

chapters.title: Corvin
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Corvin Joubert arrives in Halfway Landing aboard the flagship dredge, all charm and leverage, offering Vesper a job and a place in the family business. Vesper hides the map and declines. Beat: old wounds reopened; loyalty to a dead promise over living blood.

chapters.title: First Tide Down
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The crew runs the shallow upper river at night to avoid Corvin's patrols, nearly losing the barge on a gravel bar. Odile proves herself at the wheel and begins to suspect Vesper knows more than he says. Beat: earned respect shadowed by suspicion.

chapters.title: The Hold Beneath the Hold
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Diving the first likely site, they find not the Meridian Star but another vessel — a company barge deliberately sunk, cargo manifests intact. Someone hid things here long before Amos. Beat: the mystery deepens from treasure to cover-up.

chapters.title: Manifests and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. The recovered manifests show the Meridian Star's cargo was diverted before it ever sailed — and the signature authorizing it belongs to Vesper's father. Junie confronts Vesper privately; he admits nothing. Beat: fracture lines forming inside the found family.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Someone cuts their fuel line overnight; a day's tide is lost repairing damage. They realize one of the river camps along their route is reporting to Corvin. Paranoia sets in. Beat: the race tightening — four tides left.

chapters.title: Odile's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Corvin's men catch up and offer Odile full exoneration if she delivers Vesper's map. She burns the offer in front of the crew instead, choosing them over her own redemption. Beat: loyalty declared out loud; the crew becomes a family.

chapters.title: The Shifting Channel
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Following Amos's riddle-like annotations, Vesper finally deciphers the map: the wreck lies beneath the old oxbow, buried when the river jumped course. They anchor over it as the water drops. Beat: triumph edged with dread — three tides left.

chapters.title: What Amos Carried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Amos's POV decades earlier. As a young deckhand he watched Vesper's father order the Meridian Star scuttled — not for insurance, but to bury proof that Corvin had sold out the river communities' claims to outside investors. Beat: the truth of the inheritance revealed to the reader.

chapters.title: Two Tides
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Dredging begins on the oxbow; Corvin's flagship anchors within shouting distance, having deduced the site. Corvin boards under truce and reveals he knows Vesper is his brother's son — and offers him everything if he walks away. Beat: temptation at its strongest.

chapters.title: The Hold Opens
chapters.summary: Full-crew POV rotation. On the last safe tide they break into the Meridian Star's hold and find not gold but documents: deeds, ledgers, and sworn statements proving every river claim Corvin's fleet now works was stolen. Beat: the promise made tangible.

chapters.title: Storm Tide
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Corvin moves to seize the documents by force as a storm surge reverses the falling river. In the chaos the two vessels collide; Sefa is nearly lost overboard and saved by Junie, while the documents are nearly swept away. Beat: climax — physical peril fusing with moral stakes.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. With Corvin's ship disabled and the documents in hand, Vesper holds the power to bargain privately — keep the fortune quiet, restore his name, inherit everything. Instead he reads the ledger aloud to the gathered river crews. Beat: the promise kept; the inheritance refused.

chapters.title: Reckoning at Halfway
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. Back in town, the river communities file claims backed by the documents; investigators impound Corvin's fleet. Corvin, ruined, tells Vesper he's more his father than he knows — and Vesper finally understands it as neither insult nor absolution. Beat: justice without triumphalism.

chapters.title: A Field Worth Keeping
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The crew repairs Vesper's plane together and rebuilds the derelict airstrip at Halfway Landing as a medicine-run base. Vesper signs a lease — the longest commitment he's ever made. Beat: stopping chosen freely at last.

chapters.title: Delivered
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, final chapter. He flies Amos's ashes upriver to the trapping cabin and buries them above the oxbow, then turns south toward a full manifest and a home field waiting. The epilogue beat: the man who kept moving has somewhere to land.
